articleTitle: Ensuring inverter drives do not present a signalling safety hazard-the solution
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Ensuring Inverter Drives Do Not Present a Safety Hazard to Signalling Systems
abstract: The author describes how the essence of compatibility between any traction power electronic equipment and signalling system which share a conductive path through the running rail is based on two principles: (i) signalling frequency avoidance; and only when this is impossible, (ii) signalling frequency minimisation. In the case of inverter propulsion drives the variable frequency nature of the equipment makes the task of ensuring compatibility more complex than for other forms of drive. Consequently, the author considers AC and DC supplied equipments separately.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fail-safe design of a modern traction convertor compatible with railway track circuits
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Ensuring Inverter Drives Do Not Present a Safety Hazard to Signalling Systems
abstract: Compatibility as discussed by the author is treated by railway authorities as a safety issue. Consequentially the assessment of the proof offered by a traction manufacturer is a very careful and formal procedure and the proof he offers should be of a very high quality standard. A quality assurance system compliant with ISO 9001 at least is required to bring this procedure to a successful end. The author describes a concept which was pursued by Holec for the Class 323 EMU and focuses on safe design of the systems on the train themselves. He shows that modern traction systems require an unusual degree of filtering and design features to meet existing standards for track-circuit interference.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The problem: traction inverter drives and signalling compatibility
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Ensuring Inverter Drives Do Not Present a Safety Hazard to Signalling Systems
abstract: For the safe operation of the railway it is essential that any traction vehicles running on it, in conjunction with the power supply system do not interfere with the correct operation of the signalling system. Here, the authors consider how this problem is approached by the signalling engineer and how this may lead to a specification for permissible interference such that the signalling equipment would continue to operate safely. They also consider how this in turn presents a problem to traction designers and how the specification has developed in the light of such experience.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fail-safe traction control monitoring to ensure the safety of signalling
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Ensuring Inverter Drives Do Not Present a Safety Hazard to Signalling Systems
abstract: The author describes the development and design of the interference monitor unit (IMU). The purpose of the IMU is to provide a fail-safe monitoring system which can be built into a locomotive's traction control system to ensure that a train does not dangerously interfere with track signalling circuits. As an example the author concentrates on a single frequency interference monitor as used on British Rail (BR) Class 465 trains, but the basic unit has been designed to be able to be expanded to cover a number of frequencies, for different AC track circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
